comments.text: I workin in wildlife conservation and research. I have colleagues who work with jaguars in Belize. On an off day the student attempted to change a light bulb in the field house when a rat nest fell on him from the rafters. With in a few hours he was down and very very ill. The professor brought their student to the hospital as soon as he was sick and once there the doctor kept insisting on various diseases but the professor with over 20 years of trapping and research on small mammals immediately clocked that this was similar progression and contraction of Hantavirus. She suggested and eventually pleaded with the doctors to treat him for hanta but they (being both men and medical doctors) told her to quiet down and let the real doctors work. The students died with 24 hours of contracting hantavirus. The virus was confirmed via autopsy both in Belize and in the United States.
